text: Mahmoud has schizophrenia. His doctor suggests cognitive-behavioural therapy (CBT) to help
manage Mahmoud’s positive symptoms.
Suggest how CBT could be used to help Mahmoud manage his positive symptoms of
schizophrenia. [4]

parts.text: Outline Miller’s feeling-state theory of impulse control disorders.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain one reason why Miller’s feeling-state theory could be considered holistic.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Using the diagnostic criteria (ICD-11) for pyromania:

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Suggest one reason why Emi may be diagnosed with pyromania.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: Suggest one reason why Emi may not be diagnosed with pyromania.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
In relation to pyromania, Emi meets some of the diagnostic criteria and not others.
Explain one other problem a doctor could have when making their diagnosis of Emi.

text: Emi was unfairly dismissed from her job at a factory which she was very upset about. Afterwards,
she started a fire at the factory, which made her feel better. Later she felt very anxious and
purchased matches to relieve this anxiety. As she watched each match burn, she felt better.
Although Emi has a new job in a shop, she is distracted by thoughts of starting a fire there. These
thoughts make her feel very excited.

Describe SSRIs and exposure and response prevention (ERP).

parts.text:

Evaluate SSRIs and exposure and response prevention (ERP), including a discussion about
the use of children in research.

debates. 
Section B: Consumer Psychology

text: A shop has been receiving complaints about their virtual store layout. The shop currently has a
racetrack layout.
Suggest two ways that the shop could change their virtual store layout that could reduce
complaints. [4]

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Outline what is meant by free-will, including an example from thinking slow (system 2) in
consumer decision-making.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Explain one problem a psychologist may have when they investigate whether consumers use
free-will when deciding to purchase products.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Outline the choice heuristic used by Sally.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: Outline the choice heuristic used by Dan.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Outline one problem a psychologist may have when deciding which choice heuristic
consumers are using when purchasing a product.

text: Sally and Dan want to buy new running shoes. They go to many stores and consider lots of
different shoes. Sally returns to the first shop and buys her running shoes. Even though he has
seen many different brands, Dan buys the brand he has worn for the past few years.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Describe what psychologists have discovered about:
• gift-wrapping including beliefs of giver and recipient, and
• attention and shelf position.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:

• gift-wrapping including beliefs of giver and recipient, and
• attention and shelf position,
including a discussion about generalisations from findings.

debates.

Section D: Organisational Psychology

text: A manager has changed the working hours in a factory. Some workers are tired when they arrive
at work due to this change and have made mistakes on the production line.
Suggest how the manager could use two of Heifetz’s six principles in meeting adaptive challenges
to help the workers at the factory adjust to the change in working hours. [4]

the nature versus nurture debate.

the leaflet. Justify your answer.

text: Tricia and Margot are in a team working on a leaflet for a company. Tricia will design the leaflet.
Margot will check the leaflet for any errors before it is published.

including a discussion about individual and situational explanations.
